# watchpoint_heartbeat_monitor (Resource)

A heartbeat (cron / dead-man's-switch) monitor. Nothing is probed: a scheduled job pings `ping_url` when it succeeds, and the monitor fails when no ping arrives within `expected_period_seconds` + `grace_period_seconds`. Requires the `heartbeat_monitors` feature (any paid plan).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A nightly batch job that must check in once a day. Nothing is probed: the job
# calls ping_url when it finishes, and the monitor goes critical 10 minutes
# after a daily ping fails to arrive.
resource "watchpoint_heartbeat_monitor" "nightly_invoicing" {
  name                    = "Nightly invoicing"
  expected_period_seconds = 86400
  grace_period_seconds    = 600
  alert_profile_id        = watchpoint_alert_profile.devops.id
  tags                    = ["cron", "billing"]
}

# A five-minute worker loop, with the token rotated on a schedule. Changing
# rotate_trigger mints a new token and invalidates the old URL immediately, so
# roll it out to the job in the same apply.
resource "watchpoint_heartbeat_monitor" "queue_drainer" {
  name                    = "Queue drainer"
  expected_period_seconds = 300
  grace_period_seconds    = 120
  rotate_trigger          = "2026-q3"
}

# The ping URL embeds the token, which is the only credential on an anonymous
# endpoint. Mark every output that carries it sensitive.
output "nightly_invoicing_ping_url" {
  value     = watchpoint_heartbeat_monitor.nightly_invoicing.ping_url
  sensitive = true
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Human-readable monitor name; shown across the UI and alerts.

### Optional

- `alert_profile_id` (String) Profile that controls notification channels and routing.
- `cron_expression` (String) Five-field cron schedule the job runs on, for example `0 2 * * 1-5`. When set it replaces `expected_period_seconds` for overdue detection: a ping is expected at each scheduled run plus `grace_period_seconds`, so a weekday job stays quiet at the weekend. Six-field (seconds) cron is rejected.
- `environment_id` (String) Environment the monitor belongs to (a `watchpoint_environment` id). When omitted, a new monitor joins the tenant's default environment and an existing one keeps its environment. Reads return the effective environment, so a monitor that follows the default shows the default's id.
- `expected_period_seconds` (Number) How often the job is expected to ping, in seconds. Defaults to `3600`. Between `60` and `2592000` (30 days).
- `grace_period_seconds` (Number) Slack allowed on top of `expected_period_seconds` before the monitor is marked down, in seconds. Defaults to `300`. Between `0` and `2592000`.
- `group_id` (String) Monitor group this monitor belongs to.
- `location_profile_id` (String) Location profile recorded on the monitor. A heartbeat is not probed from a region, so this only labels where the work is expected to run.
- `rotate_trigger` (String) Arbitrary value that rotates `ping_token` when it changes. Change it (for example to a new date) to mint a fresh token in place, keeping the same `id`. The previous `ping_url` stops working immediately, so every job using it has to be updated in the same apply.
- `sla_profile_id` (String) SLA profile attached to this monitor. When omitted the monitor keeps what it has, which on create is the tenant's default SLA profile if one is set.
- `tags` (Set of String) Free-form tags surfaced in filters and SGL queries (`attributes.tags`). Unordered.
- `threshold_profile_id` (String) Profile that controls consecutive-failure logic.
- `time_zone` (String) IANA time zone `cron_expression` is evaluated in, for example `Europe/Berlin`. Defaults to UTC. Requires `cron_expression`.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp (RFC 3339).
- `id` (String) Monitor ID.
- `last_check_at` (String) Timestamp of the last ping received (RFC 3339), or null while the monitor is still waiting for its first ping. A monitor that has never pinged is never marked down.
- `last_check_status` (String) Status of the last recorded check (`Success`, `Critical`, ...), or null.
- `next_expected_at` (String) Next scheduled run the monitor is waiting on (RFC 3339, UTC), for cron schedules; null for a fixed period.
- `ping_token` (String, Sensitive) Server-minted 43-character token that authenticates the ping. It is the only credential on an anonymous endpoint, so treat it as a secret: anyone holding it can report this job as healthy.
- `ping_url` (String, Sensitive) Fully-formed URL the job calls on success (`GET` or `POST`). Append `/start` to record a start time and `/fail` to fail the check immediately without waiting out the grace period. Embeds `ping_token`, so it is equally sensitive.
- `status` (String) Current monitor status (e.g. `Active`, `Paused`). Only `Active` monitors are swept for being overdue; the others keep accepting pings without paging.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import watchpoint_heartbeat_monitor.nightly_invoicing mon_hb_001
```
